lead: Henderson plumbing deals with very hard water, desert heat and mostly newer slab homes. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Henderson.
risk: very hard water scale, water heater wear and slab leaks
risk_short: hard water, water heaters and slab leaks
why: Most Henderson homes were built since the 1990s, in Green Valley, Anthem, Seven Hills and newer areas. The issues are minerals and age: first water heaters, softeners and fixtures are wearing out.
Homes sit on slabs, so leaks under the floor happen. Summer heat in garages shortens water heater life, and strict water rules make leaks costly.
water: Henderson's water comes from Lake Mead through the Southern Nevada Water Authority. It is very hard, so scale builds up fast in heaters, tankless units and fixtures.
tips: Flush your water heater every year.
Watch your water bill for slab leak signs.
areas: PipeMend works in Green Valley, Anthem, Seven Hills, MacDonald Highlands, Inspirada, Cadence and every other Henderson neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Henderson Building and Fire Safety Department, and contractors must be licensed by the Nevada State Contractors Board.

faq.q: Why is Henderson water so hard?
faq.a: Henderson's water comes from Lake Mead, fed by the Colorado River, which carries dissolved minerals. Hard water leaves scale in heaters and on fixtures. A softener and yearly flushing help.
